events.name: The One Who Cried Smoke
events.intro:
A Torkoal is backed against a cliff by three Steel-types. It isn't fighting. It's crying, and every sob puts out a cloud of white smoke.

A Skarmory circles overhead, wings ringing like knives on a whetstone. A Magneton hums. A Lairon scrapes the ground and waits.

The cliff behind the Torkoal is covered in scorch marks. There are eleven of them, and the old ones are paler, worn down by weather. Somebody has been counting.

Hiker Caspian: "It keeps coming back. They keep beating it."
Hiker Caspian: "It cries, it sleeps, it comes back. Eleven times this year. I've stopped being able to watch."

success.text:
You walk across the valley floor and stop beside the Torkoal. It looks up at you through the smoke, astonished.

Your lead steps up on its other side. For the first time in eleven tries, the Torkoal is not alone. It stops crying long enough to plant its feet.
You put yourself between the Torkoal and the valley, and send your team at the three of them.

You crouch down and hold out a tissue. The Torkoal stares at it. Then it takes it, very carefully, in its mouth, and blows its nose.

A jet of flame roars out across the valley, white-hot and as long as a house. The Skarmory flares backwards. The Magneton's hum goes up an octave.

Everyone is impressed: Caspian, your team, and the Skarmory most of all. The Torkoal, very pleased with itself, hands back what is left of the tissue. It is ash.

Caspian presses a lump of Charcoal into your hand. "Off the cliff. It's been making them all year."

events.name: Smoke Over the Stands
events.intro:
You are still in the tunnel under the stands, waiting for your name, when the crowd starts murmuring.

A column of white smoke is rising out of your bag, straight up through the open roof, where everyone in the stadium can see it. The Torkoal is crying already.
It knows what today is.

success.text:
You walk out with it billowing round you like a cape. Somebody in the top rows starts clapping. Somebody else joins in.

By the time you reach the middle, the whole crowd knows that something out there cried eleven times and came back a twelfth.

events.name: The Dancing Crocodile
events.intro:
A Totodile is dancing on a rock in the middle of a lake. It stamps, it spins, it claps its little jaws in time to nothing at all.

Two trainers on opposite shores threw a Ball at the same moment. Both Balls are floating, bobbing gently, one on each side of the rock.

Ravenna, on the far shore: "Mine hit first."
Neither Ball has a mark on it. The Totodile dances between them, absolutely thrilled to be wanted twice.

Ravenna: "Battle for it? Or ask it?"

success.text:
Ravenna grins and wades in to her knees. "One on one. Winner keeps the dancer."
On its rock, the Totodile starts a new dance, faster, as if it were the referee.

You call across the water. The Totodile stops, one foot in the air, and looks at you. Then it dances a step and waits, head on one side.

It dances to whoever dances back. Your lead looks at you, looks at the rock, and then, because it loves you, it dances.

It is terrible. It is the best thing the Totodile has ever seen. It dives off the rock and swims straight for you, and comes up still dancing.

Ravenna laughs until she has to sit down in the shallows. "Fair. That's fair. I couldn't have done that."

You fish your own Ball out of the water and wave her on.
Ravenna stares at you for a moment as if you have done something she will need to think about later.

The Totodile hops into her Ball. Just before it goes, it turns to you and waves with both arms.

Ravenna: "I won't forget that. Find me on the road some time. I'll owe you one."

events.name: Ravenna and the Dancer
events.intro:
Two trainers block the road ahead, spoiling for a double battle. Before you can answer them, someone splashes up beside you.

Ravenna: "Told you I'd owe you one. Mind if we share?"
Her Totodile is already dancing on your side of the line.

success.text: The Totodile dances through the whole battle: between attacks, while dodging, once in the middle of a Water Gun. It does not miss a single step.

events.name: The One Who Got Too Slow
events.intro:
The one of yours that evolved most recently tries the dodge it has always done, the one that has saved it a hundred times.
It doesn't get out of the way.

It tries again in the next battle. It's hit again. Now, by the fire, it sits looking at its own feet, as if they have let it down.

A veteran by the next fire, Hargrove: "Had a Torterra like that. It kept trying to be a Grotle. You know what fixed it?"
Hargrove: "It stopped dodging. It started standing."

choices.label: Teach it to take the hit (a node).

success.text:
Hargrove gets up, groaning, and his old Torterra gets up with him. For the length of a road, the two of them spar with yours.

No dodging. Your Pokémon plants its new, heavy feet and takes the blows, and stays up, and stays up. Near the end it stops flinching.

Hargrove: "There. It's got a new shape. Now it needs a move to match."

You run it up and down the road until you are both out of breath. It is a little quicker, by the end. Only a little.

It is still unhappy. It keeps looking back at where its old self would have been.

choices.label: Tell it it's fine as it is.

success.text:
You sit down beside it and tell it so. It looks at you, and you can see it doesn't believe you yet.

But it leans against your shoulder, heavy and warm, and leaves it there.

events.name: A Move for Its Shape
events.intro:
Hargrove: "Three I'd teach a heavy one. Pick."

Your Pokémon looks up at you. Point at it again, and choose.

success.text: It goes up the rock face behind the camp in four great steps, slowly, and never once slips.
It learns to throw its whole new weight at a problem. Hargrove's Torterra rocks back a step and looks impressed.
It learns to set itself like a wall. Hargrove raps on it with his knuckles. "There. Let them hit that."

events.name: The Bird Who Wouldn't Fall
events.intro:
Rain is coming down in sheets. In the middle of an orchard, a Taillow half the size of the others is fighting an Electric-type.

It has been shocked four times. You can see it in the way its feathers stand up. It's still up. It's still diving.

Behind it, a whole ragged flock has been raiding the trees. They are thin. You can see their ribs through the wet feathers. They are starving.

Orchard keeper Brae: "I don't mind the fruit. I mind that one."
Brae: "It'll kill itself before it backs down. It doesn't know how to back down."

success.text:
You and Brae drag a crate of windfalls out under the trees. The Electric-type loses interest and wanders off. The flock comes down like rain.

They eat and eat. The small one eats last, after every other bird has had its fill, and the whole time it eats, it is watching you.
It turns on you the moment you step forward, as if it has been waiting all day for someone its own size. It won't fall. Not easily.

choices.label: Catch it before it hurts itself.

success.text:
You throw before it can dive again. The Ball shakes, and bursts open. It is out, and furious. You throw again. It breaks out a second time.

The third time, the Ball rocks once, twice, three times, and goes still. Brae lets out a breath she seems to have been holding all season.

Brae: "Good. Somebody needed to make it stop."

remembers.notice: The small Taillow lands on a branch just above you and looks at you sideways for a long time. It seems to know what you are: someone who feeds things.

success.text:
It drops onto your wrist. It is so light. Its feet are shaking with cold and with all those shocks, and it doesn't fly off.

It comes without a battle. Brae watches it go into the Ball and wipes the rain off her face, or something that isn't rain.

events.name: The Lightning Bolt
events.intro:
The storm finds you on open ground. The flash comes first, white, and in it you see your Swellow already moving.

It goes up, into the light, between the sky and your lead. The thunder comes after. When you can see again, it is on the ground, smoking, and getting up.

choices.label: Hold it until it stops shaking.

success.text: It shakes for a long time. Your lead stands over the two of you until the storm moves on. Neither of them will look away from the other all evening.

events.name: The Fire That Wouldn't Light
events.intro:
A Cyndaquil stands in front of a cold campfire, straining with its whole body. Its back smokes a little. Nothing catches.

Someone has left it a neat pile of sticks. Beside it, a young trainer is packing up his camp very slowly, like somebody who has given up waiting.

The trainer, Lysander: "It only lights when it's angry. And I don't want to make it angry."
Lysander: "I've run out of ideas. I've run out of everything."

success.text:
Lysander looks at you for a long moment. Then he holds the Ball out, relieved and sad at the same time. He asks for nothing at all.

Lysander: "It deserves someone who knows what they're doing. Its flames are out when it starts a fight. Be patient with it."

The Cyndaquil looks back at him once, and then up at you, and its back gives off one small puff of hopeful smoke.

Your Fire-type sits down beside the sticks and lights the fire slowly, one breath at a time, so the Cyndaquil can see every step.

The Cyndaquil watches. It copies the breath. Its back catches: a small blue flame, then a real one, roaring up out of its fur.

Lysander makes a noise like a laugh and a sob together. He presses a Charcoal into your hand. He won't let go of his Cyndaquil all afternoon.

You tell him it isn't about anger. You tell him to keep going. He sits back down on his pack, slowly, and looks at the sticks again.

Lysander: "All right. One more day." He gives you a Charcoal from his bag. "I won't need it if it lights. I'll need it less if it doesn't."

events.name: Lysander, Further On
events.intro: Further down the same road, a boy waves both arms at you from beside a campfire. It is Lysander, with the Cyndaquil on his shoulder.

branches.text:
Lysander: "It did it! Once! It was mostly smoke. But there was a bit of fire in the smoke."

The Cyndaquil puffs proudly. There is a little black scorch on the end of one stick, and Lysander has wrapped it in a handkerchief to keep.

success.text:
Lysander: "Look. Look!" The Cyndaquil's back is alight, steady as a lamp. It lights his fire with one breath, then lights it again, because it can.

He can't stop grinning. Neither can the Cyndaquil.

events.name: Lysander's Typhlosion
events.intro:
A crowd has gathered round a Circuit battle at the edge of town. In the middle of it, a Typhlosion stands in a ring of its own fire.

Its trainer looks up and sees you, and his whole face changes. It is Lysander, a region older. The Typhlosion's collar blazes higher.

success.text: Lysander: "Its first real fire was because of you. Let's show you what it does now."
You stay in the crowd. He wins. When he looks for you afterwards, you raise a hand, and he raises a fist with fire round it.

events.name: The Grunt's Mum
events.intro:
A woman is handing out flyers in the square. On each one is a photo of a young man in a team uniform, grinning, his hat on crooked.

The flyer says: "HAVE YOU SEEN MY SON? HE'S NOT IN TROUBLE." The last four words are underlined twice.

Mrs. Castellanos: "He said it was a job with a hat. He doesn't write. He always wrote."
Mrs. Castellanos: "I baked. I didn't know what else to do. I baked."

She is holding a tin against her chest. You know the face in the photo. You have battled him.

success.text:
She sits down on the edge of the fountain, all at once, like a puppet with its strings cut. She doesn't cry. She just breathes for a while.

Mrs. Castellanos: "All right. All right is all I wanted." She opens the tin and makes you take a biscuit. It is a Berry biscuit, still a little warm.

She presses the tin into your hands and holds on to it a moment longer than she needs to.

Mrs. Castellanos: "Tell him I'm not angry. Tell him there are more where these came from." She gives you a biscuit from the top, for the road.
It tastes of Berries.

choices.label: Tell her what the job is.

success.text:
You tell her. All of it: the stolen Pokémon, the uniforms, the cages. She doesn't interrupt once.

She goes very quiet. Then she folds the rest of her flyers, neatly, and puts them in her bag. She gives you a biscuit, very politely.

Mrs. Castellanos: "Thank you. Now. Where is this Hideout?"

events.name: Your Mum Sent These
events.intro:
A Grunt steps out across the path, Ball already in his hand. It is him: the face from the flyer, under the crooked hat.

Grunt: "You again. Right. Let's get this over wi..." Then he sees what you are holding out.

success.text:
He takes the tin in both hands. He opens it and looks inside, and his face folds up like a child's.

He can't battle. He sits down in the road and cries into the biscuits, and you sit with him until he can breathe.
When you go, he is still holding the tin.

events.name: The Bakery in the Next Region
events.intro:
A new bakery on the corner. In the window, a young man in a floury apron is setting out trays of Berry biscuits.

He has the hat on, the team hat, turned backwards and covered in flour. He sees you through the glass and goes red to the ears.

choices.label: Go in and buy a biscuit.

success.text: He won't take your money. He puts two in the bag instead of one. "Mum's recipe," he says, and doesn't say anything else, and doesn't need to.

events.name: The Team's Recruitment Fair
events.intro:
A cheerful stall in the market square, hung with balloons. The banner reads "CAREERS IN LOGISTICS. FREE HAT." A queue of teenagers stretches round the corner.

Recruiter, smiling with every tooth: "Travel. Purpose. A family. Sign here, here and here."

You pick up a contract from the pile. The first two pages are all smiles and pictures. The third page is in very small print.

success.text:
You clear your throat and read it out, loud enough for the back of the queue. "'The undersigned gives up their Pokémon to the organisation.'"

There is a silence. A girl at the front looks down at the Eevee in her arms. Then the queue leaves, all of it, quickly and without a word.

The Recruiter is still smiling. It is a very different smile. Someone from the queue presses one of the free hats into your hand on the way past.

You sign: here, here and here. The Recruiter shakes your hand warmly and gives you a uniform that almost fits, and the free hat.

For the length of a road you are one of them. You learn the passwords, the shift times, which door is never locked. You learn which room nobody guards.
The balloons go up. The table goes over. Contracts go everywhere. Two Recruiters drop the smiles and reach for their Balls.

events.name: The Ranger Trainee
events.intro:
A Ranger trainee in a uniform that is too new is clearing a fallen branch off the road. She looks up, and goes pink.

Trainee: "You won't remember me. I was in a queue. I had a pen in my hand. You read something out."

success.text: She doesn't believe you, and it doesn't matter. She salutes, badly, and lets your party past first.

events.name: The Boss's Day in Court
events.intro:
A courtroom, wood-panelled and much too warm. The team's boss sits at the front in a very good suit, hands folded, looking rested.

The gallery is packed. Nearly everyone has a Pokémon on their lap: some of them were in the cages under the Hideout, and their people are holding them very tight.

Judge: "The court calls a witness."
The boss turns, finds you, and smiles pleasantly. "Be accurate. That's all I ask."

success.text:
You tell it all, from the first whisper to the last door. Some of it you saw. Some of it you were told by people too frightened to come.

The lawyers object. The hearsay is struck out, line by line. But the rest sticks, and there is a great deal of the rest.

Judge: "Guilty." The gallery doesn't cheer. A Growlithe on someone's lap barks once, and its owner lets it.

branches.text:
You tell only what you saw. It is short, and exact, and it is not quite enough: there is too little in the Files to hold it up.

Judge: "Not proven." The boss stands, buttons his jacket, and nods to you on his way out.

success.text:
You tell only what you saw with your own eyes. It is short. It is exact. You don't look at the boss once.

It is enough. The Files back up every word. Judge: "Guilty." The boss inclines his head to you, as if you have both played well.

choices.label: Speak for the Grunts who left.

success.text:
You tell the court about the ones who walked away. The Grunt with the tin. The ones who opened doors for you.
The ones who were sixteen and wanted a hat.

The court goes easy on them. The boss watches you the whole time, and at the end his face has something in it like respect.

remembers.notice:
The boss's lawyer stands before you can begin. "The witness has lied before, on this very road. The court will remember it." Your word counts for less now.
The Files will need one more entry.

branches.text: You tell only what you saw. It is not enough, not from you, not now. Judge: "Not proven." The boss leaves by the front door.

success.text:
You tell only what you saw. It is short, and exact, and the lawyer picks at every word.

The Files hold. Just. Judge: "Guilty." The boss looks at you as if he will remember that you nearly cost him nothing.

events.name: The Stolen Pokémon That Won't Come Home
events.intro:
A girl is kneeling by the fire with her arms held out.
In front of her, a Growlithe that was stolen from her, and freed today, is hiding behind your legs.

The girl, Posy-Rae: "Pepper? It's me. Pepper, it's me."
The Growlithe shakes. It was in the pen a long time. It has learned that hands reaching for it mean the bad kind of Ball.

choices.label: Give it time. Sit down, all of us (a node).

success.text:
You sit down. Posy-Rae sits down. Your whole team sits down. She talks about nothing: what she had for breakfast, a dream about a boat, the rain.

It takes the length of a road. Bit by bit, the Growlithe creeps over on its belly, nose first, until its nose touches her knee. She keeps talking.
Her voice only wobbles once.

When it finally climbs into her lap, she gives you the Fire Stone she was saving for it. "It doesn't need to change. It just needed to come back."

You pick it up. It lets you. It is all bones and fur and it is rigid in your arms.

You put it in hers. It is stiff, stiff, and then, all at once, it is not. It pushes its whole face into her neck.
She gives you her Fire Stone without looking away from it.

choices.label: Let it stay with me a while.

success.text:
Posy-Rae: "Will you bring it home? When it's ready?" You promise. She ties her own ribbon round its neck and lets you go.

The Growlithe walks out of the camp pressed against your boot. It will travel with you for a stage, and decide for itself.

events.name: Pepper Leads the Way
events.intro:
In the morning the Growlithe with the ribbon is already up, waiting at the edge of the camp, tail going.

It has decided. It sets off without you, looks back, and waits.
You follow it for a long time, down roads you didn't plan to take, until a small house with a blue door.

success.text:
Posy-Rae opens it. The Growlithe goes past her like a shot, into the house, round the kitchen twice, and back into her arms.

She is crying too hard to speak. She puts the Fire Stone she was saving into your hand, and closes your fingers over it.

choices.label: Tell her how it got lost.

success.text:
Pepper is not with you any more, and you tell Posy-Rae the truth about that. She listens to all of it.
Then she thanks you for bringing her the truth, at least.

events.name: Two Teams, One Target
events.intro:
Two sets of Grunts in two different uniforms are robbing the same museum.
They came in from different doors, quietly, and have just met in the middle, beside the glass case.

Grunt A: "We were here first."
Grunt B: "We have a schedule."
Grunt A: "We have a better schedule."

The curator is under a desk, watching it all like a tennis match. Both crews have just noticed you in the doorway.

success.text: They both turn on you at once. The first crew is nearer.

You tell Grunt A one true thing his rivals did to his team last month. You tell Grunt B one true thing the other lot did to theirs.
Both are in the Files.

There is a long, dangerous pause. Then they are at each other: Balls, fists, a very old vase. The relic is completely forgotten.

You and the curator carry the glass case out of the side door together. Neither crew notices. She shakes your hand, then gives you something from the museum's own stores.

Your Pokémon drags both heavy doors shut and seals them. The two crews are locked in a room with each other and nothing to steal.

For the rest of the day you can hear them shouting from three roads away. The police are very, very pleased.

The curator comes out from under the desk, dusts herself down, and gives you something from the museum's own stores.

events.name: The Second Crew
events.intro: The first crew runs for its door. The second crew is still standing by the glass case, and it has watched everything you did.

success.text: They come at you in a line.

events.name: The Curator's Report
events.intro: A radio is playing in a café. The newsreader is reading out a museum report, word for word. It is extremely dry.

success.text:
"At approximately eleven, two criminal organisations entered the building to steal the same object. This was inefficient of them."

The whole café is laughing by the end. You catch yourself in the report, as "a passing trainer, unhurried."

events.name: The Trade Across a Fence
events.intro:
Two children are kneeling on opposite sides of a tall border fence, red in the face.
They are trying to push a Poké Ball through a gap that is far too small for it.

Teodoro: "My Sandshrew for her Vulpix. We agreed. The fence didn't."
Ingeborg: "Could you walk them round? It's four miles. My mum won't let me go that far."

They look at you as if you are the answer to everything.
Both of them are holding their Poké Balls very carefully, the way you do with something you have promised away.

success.text:
You take a Poké Ball from each of them and set off along the fence. Four miles, there and back, and the fence never ends.

When you hand the Balls over, both of them cheer so loudly that a Pidgey falls off the fence.
They swap addresses through the gap and promise to write every week.

Teodoro presses a Fire Stone into your hand. Ingeborg pushes an Ice Stone through the gap after it. "From both of us," they say together.

choices.label: Trade with one of them myself.

success.text:
You crouch down by the fence. Maybe you could make one of them a better offer, and save the long walk for someone.

They look at each other through the wire. "We still want ours done," says Ingeborg. "But you can ask."

Your Flying-type takes one Ball in its claws, then comes back for the other. Up, over, down, as gentle as anything.

Both children burst into applause. A few grown-ups watching from a garden join in. Your Pokémon lands looking enormously pleased with itself.

Teodoro gives you a Fire Stone. Ingeborg pushes an Ice Stone through the gap. "One from each of us. That was the best thing I've ever seen."

events.name: A Better Offer
events.intro:
Teodoro holds up his Sandshrew. It is curled into a tight ball, peeking out at you. "It digs. Everywhere. Mum's garden is all holes."

Ingeborg holds up her Vulpix. It is warm even through the Poké Ball. "She's always warm. It's nice in winter."

Whichever you take, the other one still waits for their swap. They make you promise to tell the other one where it went.

choices.label: Trade with Teodoro for his Sandshrew.

success.text:
Teodoro looks at your Pokémon for a long time, then nods, very seriously, and hands his Sandshrew over the fence the long way: up, and over, and into your arms.
It immediately tries to dig into your coat.

gives.why: It digs. Everywhere. It needs somewhere bigger than a garden.

choices.label: Trade with Ingeborg for her Vulpix.

success.text:
Ingeborg hugs her Vulpix, once, hard, then lifts it over the fence to you. It is as warm as a cup of tea.
It settles into your arms as if it has always been there.

gives.why: She's always warm. She should see the world, not just my garden.

success.text: You tell them it was their trade first, and it should stay theirs. They both look very relieved.

events.name: A Letter With a Drawing
events.intro:
A letter finds you at a rest stop, addressed in two different handwritings, one large and one very neat.

Teodoro's Sandshrew has evolved. Ingeborg's Vulpix keeps his whole house warm now. They still write every week, through the fence.

Folded inside is a drawing: two children, a very long fence, and a small figure that must be you, walking along it with a Poké Ball in each hand.

success.text: You fold it carefully and put it somewhere safe. It is not a good drawing. It is the best one you have.

events.name: The Grandmother's Collection
events.intro:
A small parlour, warm and dim. Thirty Poké Balls sit on thirty lace doilies on every surface: the mantel, the piano, the windowsill.
Each has a paper label in careful, looping handwriting.

Grandmother Eulalia: "My late husband's. All of them. I can't walk them all any more, dear. My knees."
Eulalia: "They should go to people who'll go places. One each. And you must tell me where you'll take it."

success.text: She takes you round the room, one Ball at a time, telling you each name. She stops at three of them and waits.

choices.label: Take none; walk them for her today (a node).

success.text:
You offer to walk them. All of them. She looks at you as if you have offered her the moon.

Thirty Pokémon on thirty leads, in a small village, all at once. It is chaos. A Doduo goes through a hedge. A Lickitung licks the postman.
Nobody, at any point, is in charge.

When you bring them home at dusk, every one of them is tired and happy, and so is she.

"Ask about him?" She sits down, slowly, and smiles at the nearest Ball. "Nobody asks."

"He named every one of them after a railway station. Paddington. Waverley. Euston. He liked trains.
He liked the idea that you could get on one and go anywhere at all."

"He never went anywhere. Not once. That's why they should." She looks at you. "Would you like to pick one, dear?"

events.name: Three on the Mantel
events.intro:
Three Balls on the mantel, side by side, their labels turned to face you: Paddington, Waverley, Euston.

"These three liked him best," says Eulalia. "They know their moves the old way. He taught them himself, out of a book older than me."

success.text:
Eulalia lifts the Ball off its doily and holds it a moment. "He named it after a station." She puts it in your hands. "Now. Where will you take it?"

You tell her: {nextRegion}. She writes it down on the label, under the name, in her careful hand. "Good. He always wanted to go there."

gives.why: He named it after a station. It ran the platform every morning to meet his train.

success.text:
Eulalia lifts the Ball off its doily and holds it a moment. "Waverley." She puts it in your hands. "Now. Where will you take it?"

You tell her: {nextRegion}. She writes it down on the label, under the name, in her careful hand. "Good. He always wanted to go there."

gives.why: Waverley. He liked trains. It liked him. It still waits by the door at six.

success.text:
Eulalia lifts the Ball off its doily and holds it a moment. "Euston." She puts it in your hands. "Now. Where will you take it?"

You tell her: {nextRegion}. She writes it down on the label, under the name, in her careful hand. "Good. He always wanted to go there."

gives.why: Euston. It sang him to sleep for forty years. It needs someone new to sing to.

choices.label: I can't take one from you.

success.text: She pats your hand. "That's why you could have." She puts the kettle on instead, and you stay for tea.

events.name: A Card for Eulalia
events.intro:
You are here. {nextRegion} was a name on a paper label, in looping handwriting, and now it is the ground under your feet.

There is a little shop by the station selling postcards of the trains.

success.text:
You buy the one with the biggest train on it and write on the back: "We made it." You let your Pokémon put its footprint in the corner.

Weeks later a parcel catches up with you: a knitted scarf in railway colours, far too long, with a note. "He would have been so pleased. So am I."
You don't send anything. But you look at the trains for a long time, and your Pokémon looks with you.

events.name: The Trade That Goes Wrong Honestly
events.intro:
At the edge of the market a man in a wide-brimmed hat is trying to hand a Poké Ball back to a trader.
The trader, very politely, will not take it.

Florentyn: "It doesn't like me. Three days. It sits facing the wall. It won't even eat if I'm in the room."
Ivo Ternary: "The Trade-Back is for seven days, sir. It's been three. Give it four more."

Ivo glances at you, and then, quietly: "Or someone it does like could take it."

success.text:
Ivo sets the Honest Card on his table: your Pokémon on one side, the Houndour on the other, and the fair value of each, plain for anyone to read.

Florentyn looks at it for a long time. "It isn't a bad Pokémon," he says. "I think it was just let down before."
He hands it over, and lifts his hat to it, sadly.

gives.why: It faces the wall. It was let down before, and it is waiting to see if you will too.

success.text:
You spend the afternoon with them both, in a quiet yard behind the market. Houndour sits facing the wall, the whole time.

Then you notice: it flinches every time Florentyn turns his head. Not at him. At the hat. Its last owner, Ivo tells you, wore one just like it.

Florentyn takes the hat off. Houndour turns round, slowly, and looks at him properly for the first time. Then it walks over and puts its head on his knee.

You leave them to it. Ivo keeps his word: on day seven, Houndour is traded back, and Ivo finds it someone who doesn't wear hats. You hear about it later.
It is doing well.

events.name: The Houndour in the Hat
events.intro:
On a busy street you see them again: Florentyn, bareheaded, walking with a spring in his step, and beside him a Houndour trotting proudly along.

The Houndour is wearing the hat. It is far too big for it. Nobody has the heart to tell it.

success.text: Florentyn waves back with his whole arm. The Houndour does not wave. But it does stop, and look at you, and wag once.

events.name: The Blind Trade Booth
events.intro:
A booth with a heavy velvet curtain and a hand-painted sign: BLIND SWAP. YOU DON'T SEE. THEY DON'T SEE. ODDS ON THE BOARD.

Quintessa: "The board's the law, love. You put one in, you get one out, from the pool on the board."
Quintessa: "And before you say yes, you see what's coming. Nature, quirk, the lot. I'm blind, not crooked."

success.text:
You pass a Poké Ball through the curtain. Somewhere behind it, a hand takes it, and another hand pushes a different Ball back out.

Quintessa lays the Honest Card on the counter first: what went in, what is coming out, its nature, its quirk, and the fair value of both. "Last chance, love."

The board is chalked in a careful hand. Common, the most likely. Uncommon, less so. Rare, now and then. Very rare, almost never, but not never.

Every name in the pool is written there, with its chance next to it. Nothing is hidden. Nothing is rubbed out.

Quintessa watches you read all of it. "Most people don't," she says. "They should."

choices.label: Ask who else is in the booth.

success.text:
"Today? A farmer, a sailor," Quintessa says, and then, with a little smile, "and a young trainer who looked a lot like you. Same look in the eye."

Your rival. Somewhere behind that curtain is one of your rival's own Pokémon. If it comes out, it will know you.

events.name: The Booth, Again
events.intro: The curtain stirs. Quintessa taps the counter. "Well, love? In or out?"

success.text: You pass a Poké Ball through the curtain. Quintessa lays the Honest Card on the counter before anything else. "Look at it properly. Then decide."
You thank her and walk on. Behind you, the curtain sways, and somebody else steps up to try their luck.

events.name: Doing Well
events.intro:
At a crossroads you pass a farmer with a cart, and riding on top of the hay, looking very at home, is the Pokémon you put through the curtain.

It sees you. It doesn't jump down. But it watches you all the way past, and it looks well. It looks happy.

success.text: You raise a hand. The farmer, puzzled, raises one back. The Pokémon settles down in the hay again, exactly where it belongs now.

events.name: The Last Trade of a Retiring Trader
events.intro:
A trader's cart stands at the roadside with everything marked down to almost nothing, and a hand-painted sign nailed to the side: FORTY YEARS. LAST DAY.

Trader Balthasar: "I've one left I never could trade. Forty years. Nobody wanted it."
Balthasar: "I'm not selling it. I'm placing it. There's a difference."

On the cart's seat, holding the reins in its wings as if it is the one driving, sits a very old Farfetch'd.
It looks at you over its leek like a magistrate.

success.text:
Balthasar sets the Honest Card on the seat: nothing on your side at all. On his, the old Farfetch'd, every year of it written down.

"It's slow," he says. "It's clever. It's been on every road in this region twice."
The Farfetch'd gets down off the cart, looks back once, and walks over to stand beside you.

Balthasar watches it go. He doesn't say anything else. He doesn't have to.

gives.why: It's slow. It's clever. Nobody wanted it, and it was the best of the lot.

success.text:
Balthasar looks at the Farfetch'd. The Farfetch'd looks at Balthasar.

"It bit a duke," he says. "In nineteen-something. Word gets round."

The Farfetch'd does not look sorry in the least.

choices.label: Offer to take the cart, too.

success.text:
He laughs. He laughs for a long time, leaning on the cart, wiping his eyes.

Then he reaches up and unhooks the little brass bell from the front of it, and puts it in your hand.
"Forty years that rang every time I got a good deal. Let it ring for you now."

events.name: The Cart Seat
events.intro: The old Farfetch'd is still on the cart seat, still holding the reins. Balthasar waits.

success.text:
Balthasar sets the Honest Card on the seat, nothing on your side of it.
The Farfetch'd climbs down, slow and careful, and comes to stand beside you as if it always meant to.

gives.why: It's slow. It's clever. Nobody wanted it, and it was the best of the lot.

success.text: "No," says Balthasar, when you say it should stay with him. "But thank you." He climbs up beside it, and they drive off together, slowly, into the last day.

events.name: Balthasar at the Inn
events.intro:
In the corner of an inn, at a table by the fire, sits Balthasar. He has a cup of tea in front of him and nobody to trade with.

He is giving advice to a young trader at the next table, who did not ask for it, about the price of Pecha Berries in a dry year.
He is enjoying himself enormously.

success.text:
He sees you and lights up. You hear about the duke. You hear about all forty years.
You leave much later than you meant to, and it is worth every minute.

events.name: The Town With One Clock
events.intro:
Everyone in the square is standing still, looking up at the town clock. It has stopped. They are arguing about what time it is.

Baker: "It's dawn. I've baked."
Lamplighter: "It's dusk. I've lit."
A child: "It's lunch. I'm hungry."

Clock-keeper Ottokar, on a ladder against the clock face: "A Klink's gone from the works. Walked out. I think it was bored."

success.text:
You find it at the fair at the bottom of the hill, riding the carousel, round and round, with an expression of total peace.

It will come back, you explain to Ottokar, if it gets Sundays off. He stands at the bottom of the ladder for a long time. Then he agrees.

The clock starts with a clank. The whole town checks it. Ottokar gives you a bed for the night, and a pocket watch set to the right time.

choices.label: Lend a Pokémon to the works (a node).

success.text:
Your Pokémon climbs into the works behind the clock face and takes hold of the big gear. It turns. The hands move. The square cheers.

For a whole day the town runs on its mood. When it is cheerful the hours fly. When it gets bored the afternoon lasts forever. Nobody minds.

Ottokar gives you a bed for the night and a pocket watch, and your Pokémon comes out of the works oily and proud.

You look at the sun and tell them, quite reasonably, what time it is.

Nobody believes a stranger. The baker goes back to his ovens and the lamplighter goes back to his lamps. The clock stays stopped.

events.name: Closed Sundays
events.intro:
You pass back through a town you remember. The clock is running. Under it, a small sign has been screwed to the wall.

"CLOSED SUNDAYS. THE KLINK IS AT THE FAIR."

choices.label: Check your pocket watch against it.

success.text: They match, to the second, except that both are an hour out. Nobody here minds at all.

events.name: The Ferryman's Last Crossing
events.intro:
A new bridge is being opened today. There are ribbons, and a band, and a mayor with very large scissors.

Fifty metres downstream, a ferryman sits in his boat with nobody in it. He is watching the ribbons, and his face is very still.

Ferryman Lorcan: "Forty years. I know every stone in this river. Tomorrow nobody needs that."
Lorcan: "One more across? No charge."

success.text:
You step down into the boat.
He pushes off, and as he rows, he tells you the river: where it floods in spring, which stones move, where the current lies about itself.

Halfway over he stops rowing and points down. Far below, in a deep green pool, something long and blue is curled up asleep. "Dratini. Every winter. Nobody knows but me.
And you."

On the far bank there is a path you would never have seen from the bridge. In the shallows by the landing, a scale glints.
He tells you to keep it.

You walk over the new bridge with the crowd. The mayor shakes your hand, hard, for the photographer, and says you are the future.

From the middle of the bridge you can see the ferry, still tied up, and the ferryman, still sitting in it.

He thinks about it for a long time, as if nobody has asked.

Lorcan: "Teach kids the river, maybe. If anyone asks." He looks at the bridge. "Nobody will ask."

events.name: The Crossing
events.intro: The band starts up on the bridge. Lorcan picks up his oars, and puts them down again, and waits to see which way you go.

success.text:
You step down into the boat. As he rows, he tells you the river: where it floods, which stones move. Halfway over he points down at a deep pool. "Dratini.
Every winter."

On the far bank there is a path you would never have seen from the bridge. In the shallows by the landing, a scale glints.
He tells you to keep it.
You walk over the bridge with the crowd. The mayor shakes your hand for the photographer. The ferry stays tied up below.

events.name: The Letter for a House That's Gone
events.intro:
A postman is standing in the middle of a field, holding a letter, looking at a chimney. There is no house round it. There hasn't been for a long time.

Postman Mr. Abara: "Forty-two Elm. There's an elm. There's a chimney."
Mr. Abara: "It's marked urgent. Thirty years ago. It fell behind a sorting frame."

Mr. Abara: "I can't open it. Rules. Thirty years and I've never broken one. I don't know what to do."

success.text:
He hands it to you and turns his back, so that he hasn't technically seen. You open it. It is one line, in a hand that shakes.

"I forgive you. Come home."

Nobody knows who to. Nobody knows from whom. Mr. Abara stands in the field for a long time.
Then he gives you his spare whistle, because he doesn't know what else to do.

You ask in every house down the lane. An old man remembers the fire. A woman remembers the name. A boy remembers where they went.

The granddaughter runs the inn in the next village. She reads the letter twice, standing at the bar, and then sits down on the floor behind it.

When she can talk, she gives you both a room for the night and won't hear a word about paying. Mr. Abara writes "DELIVERED" in his book with enormous care.

You prop the letter in the hearth, out of the rain. Mr. Abara nods slowly. It is, at least, the address.

A Hoothoot drops out of the chimney, looks at the letter, and takes it back up inside, where it lives. Mr.
Abara gives you his spare whistle and goes off whistling on his own.

events.name: Forty-Two Elm
events.intro: You stop at an inn you know. The sign over the door has been taken down and repainted. In new gold letters it reads: "Forty-Two Elm."

success.text: The granddaughter is behind the bar. She points at a frame on the wall: the letter, under glass. She pours you a drink and won't take your money, again.

events.name: The Boy Who Sells Directions
events.intro:
A boy sits on a milestone at a crossroads, swinging his legs, beside a hand-drawn sign: "DIRECTIONS ₽10. GOOD DIRECTIONS ₽50."

The boy, Ferdinand: "The ₽10 ones are true. The ₽50 ones are true and nice."

His shoes are held together with string. He has drawn a very careful map on the back of the sign, with little trees on it.

success.text:
He takes the coin and bites it, like he's seen someone do.

Ferdinand: "Left." He points left. It is the right way.

Ferdinand: "Left, and there's a Berry tree at the bend, and the dog at the farm's friendly, and it gets pretty at the top."

All of it is true. The tree is there, heavy with Berries. The dog is friendly.
And at the top of the hill there is a spot so pretty that you stop, and sit, and rest.

He looks at his shoes.

Ferdinand: "Saving for a Poké Ball. There's a Pidgey at the farm that likes me. I'm ₽40 short. I've been ₽40 short for a month."

events.name: Forty Short
events.intro: Ferdinand is pretending very hard that he didn't just tell you that.

success.text:
You put a Poké Ball in his hands. He holds it like it might break.

Ferdinand: "I'll pay you back. In directions. Forever." He is already running toward the farm.
He counts it three times. Then he runs, all the way down the road to the shop and back, with the Ball held over his head like a trophy.

He sells you the ₽50 ones, very seriously. There is a Berry tree at the bend. The dog is friendly. It gets pretty at the top.

You stop at the top, and sit, and rest. When you look back down, he is counting the money again.

events.name: Free Directions
events.intro:
On the next route there is a boy at a fork with a Pidgey on his head. His sign has been painted over.

It says: "DIRECTIONS. FREE."

success.text: Ferdinand: "Left. And there's a Berry tree at the bend." The Pidgey points with its whole wing, in case you missed it.

events.name: The Widow's Scarecrow
events.intro:
A scarecrow stands in a field of corn, wearing a good suit. The suit is a little too big for it. A woman is straightening its tie.

Farmer Griselda: "His. His good suit. He'd have hated it out here."
Griselda: "The crows liked him too, so it doesn't work."

A Murkrow is sitting on the scarecrow's shoulder, very comfortably, as if it owns the place.

success.text:
Your Pokémon charges into the corn. The crows go up in a great black sheet and away over the hedge.

All but one. The Murkrow won't go. It moves along the scarecrow's arm, out of reach, and settles again. Griselda doesn't try to shift it.

Griselda: "It was his. It used to sit on his shoulder just like that. While he worked." She fills a sack with corn for you anyway.

She tells you. Fifty years in this field. Bad knees. A laugh you could hear from the road.

Griselda: "He talked to that bird more than he talked to me. I talk to it now." The Murkrow cocks its head at her.
She fills a sack with corn for you.
You lift a hand and walk on. She waves, and goes back to the tie, and the Murkrow watches you to the end of the field.

events.name: Plant Enough for Both
events.intro: The Murkrow is still there, on his shoulder, in his good suit. Griselda is looking at it the way you look at an old photograph.

choices.label: "It can stay. Plant enough for both."

success.text:
She looks at you. Then she laughs: a real one, surprised out of her, the first in a long time, you can tell.

Griselda: "He said that. Every spring. Word for word." She is still laughing, and wiping her eyes, when you leave.
You leave the two of them in the field: the woman and the bird, and the suit between them.

events.name: Two Scarecrows
events.intro: It is harvest time in a field you remember. There are two scarecrows now: one in a good suit, one in a flowered dress. The crows sit on both.

success.text: Someone waves back from the porch. On the porch rail sits a Murkrow, eating corn from a bowl.

events.name: The Funeral in the Tall Grass
events.intro:
You expected a wild battle. Instead, a ring of wild Pokémon of a dozen different kinds is standing round something small in the grass. Predators and prey, side by side.
None of them moves.

It is an old Raticate, grey round the muzzle, very still. A Fearow, of all things, has brought a flower, and laid it down with its terrible beak.

They notice you. Nobody runs.

choices.label: Take off my hat and wait (a node).

success.text:
You take off your hat and stand at the edge of the ring. Your team stands with you. Nobody says anything, because nobody there can.

It takes a long time. One by one, they go back into the grass. The Fearow goes last but one, and nods to you as it passes.

The very last is a young Rattata. It sits beside the old one for a while. Then it looks at you, a long look, and goes.
You step into the ring and leave a Berry by the flower. The Fearow watches you do it. Then it nods to you, once, slow and grave.
You back away, quietly, the way you would leave a room where somebody is sleeping. They watch you go, every one of them, until the grass closes.
You send your lead in. The ring breaks. The Fearow turns on you with a scream that has nothing in it but grief.

events.name: The Young Rattata
events.intro:
A young Rattata is sitting in the middle of the road, as if it has been waiting. You know it.
It looked at you once, for a long time, over something small in the grass.

choices.label: Crouch down and hold out a hand.

success.text: It sniffs your fingers, and then your boots, and then the whole of your team. Then it climbs into your bag as if it has decided something.

choices.label: Let it go its own way.

success.text: It watches you pass, and then goes off into the grass, upright and certain, the way the old one must have walked.

events.name: The Teacher in the Stream
events.intro:
A Poliwrath stands waist-deep in a clear stream. In front of it, in a row, float seven Poliwag.

It does a stroke, slow and perfect. They copy it, badly, all splash and spin. It does the stroke again. They copy it again, a little less badly.

One Poliwag keeps drifting off downstream. The Poliwrath wades over and fetches it back, without a trace of impatience. You count. It does this nine times.

success.text: You sit on the bank with your boots off and watch the whole lesson to the end. It is the most restful thing you have seen in days.

choices.label: Let my Water-type join the class.

success.text:
Your Water-type slides into the stream at the end of the row. The Poliwrath looks it up and down, and then teaches it exactly as patiently as the others.

By the end, your Pokémon has learned something. You can see it in how it moves.

You wade in and catch the drifter. It isn't drifting. It is watching fish, and birds, and the way the light moves on the water.
It wants to be something else.

When you climb out of the stream, it climbs out after you. The Poliwrath watches, and does not fetch it back this time.

events.name: What It Learned
events.intro: Which lesson stuck? Point at your Water-type again.

success.text: It learned to swim up, against the whole weight of the stream.
It learned to go from still to gone in one kick.

events.name: On the Bank
events.intro: Your Politoed hops ahead onto a riverbank and stops. On the far side, waist-deep, stands a Poliwrath with a row of Poliwag in front of it.

choices.label: Wait while they look at each other.

success.text: The Poliwrath looks at the Politoed for a long time. Then it turns back to its class. Your Politoed sings the whole way to the next town.

events.name: The Border Dispute
events.intro:
A line of Sentret stands on one side of a fallen log. A line of Zigzagoon stands on the other.
On the log, exactly in the middle, sits a single Oran Berry.

You step out of the trees. Both sides start chattering at you at once, pointing at the Berry, at each other, at the sky.

Each side clearly thinks you have been sent to judge.

success.text:
You cut it exactly in half with great ceremony and give one half to each side.

Both sides are dissatisfied, loudly and equally. And so the peace holds.

choices.label: Give them each one of mine.

success.text:
You take two Oran Berries from your bag and set one on each side of the log.

There is a long, suspicious silence. Then peace. The original Berry stays on the log, untouched, a monument. A Sentret and a Zigzagoon stay behind to see you off.
You pick up the Berry and eat it. Both sides go silent. Then, for the first time in history, Sentret and Zigzagoon are united, against you.

events.name: The Envoy
events.intro: Two small figures are still standing by the log: a Sentret and a Zigzagoon, side by side, chests out. Envoys. Each would like to go with you.

success.text: The Sentret stands up very tall and marches over. The Zigzagoon zigzags off to report.
The Zigzagoon runs to you in a perfect zigzag. The Sentret stands up very tall and salutes.
You thank them both, very formally. They bow, very formally, and go back to their own sides of the log.

events.name: The Mixed Patrol
events.intro: A patrol trots across the road ahead of you: two Sentret, two Zigzagoon, in step. They stop, look at you, and give you a long, hard look.

success.text: They salute back, all four of them, and march on into the trees. One of them is carrying an Oran Berry.

events.name: The Night the Stars Fell Into the Lake
events.intro:
The lake is full of light. Hundreds of Staryu and Starmie are rising to the surface at once, their cores blinking, red and gold and white.

Overhead, a meteor shower is passing. They are answering it. Each streak in the sky gets a blink in the water.

A night fisher, Eudora: "Once a decade. They think it's their relations." She hasn't touched her rod. "I've seen it three times. I've cried three times."

success.text:
You sit down on the shore with your whole team and watch until the last star has gone.

Nobody says anything. Nobody needs to. When the lake goes dark, your Pokémon are all leaning on you, and on each other.

Eudora fishes a Star Piece out of the shallows and gives it to you without a word.

branches.text:
You blink your torch at the lake: once, twice, once. Then the whole lake blinks back, and for a minute you are part of it.

Something small and sleepy, far above, wakes up and hears you. Eudora gives you a Star Piece. "They'll remember you now."

success.text:
You blink your torch at the lake: once, twice, once. For a moment nothing happens.

Then the whole lake blinks back. Once, twice, once. For a minute you are part of it: the sky, the water, and you, between them, answering.

Something high above, far past the meteors, takes notice of that. Eudora gives you a Star Piece. "They'll remember you now."

You wade in up to your knees. The lights swirl round your legs, warm, humming.

When you wade out again, one Staryu has attached itself firmly to your bag, and it will not let go.
Eudora laughs and gives you a Star Piece for it to look at.

events.name: The First Blink
events.intro: A clear night. Far off, on a lake you can barely see, one light blinks. Once, twice, once. It blinks first.

success.text: You blink your torch at it. Once, twice, once. The far light answers, and goes out, satisfied. You sleep better than you have in weeks.

events.name: The Bully of the Watering Hole
events.intro:
There is one water hole for miles, and one tree beside it. A Pangoro sits in the only shade, by the only water. Everything else waits in the sun.

A Skiddo creeps forward, tongue out, desperate. The Pangoro growls. The Skiddo goes back.

The Pangoro has a leaf in its mouth, and it is chewing it hard. When it shifts its weight, it does it carefully. It has a limp it is hiding.

success.text: It comes out of the shade at you like a landslide. It fights hard, and badly, favouring the leg.

You walk into the shade slowly, hands open. It growls the whole way. It doesn't get up. You kneel down by the leg.

A thorn, long as your finger, driven deep into the pad. You are the first thing in days that it has let close enough to see.
You pull it out in one go.

It is ashamed afterwards. It won't look at you. And then it gets up, and limps along, and moves over. The Skiddo comes down to drink.

choices.label: Bring water to the others (a node).

success.text:
You and your Water-type spend the length of a road carrying water out into the sun, to the ones waiting. Skiddo, a pair of Phanpy, things too small to name.

The Pangoro watches the whole time. Gradually, a little at a time, it shifts along the trunk, until there is shade for two, then four.

events.name: It Moves Over
events.intro:
The Pangoro is sitting at the edge of the shade now, between the water and the open savanna, where something hungry would have to get past it.
It looks at you.

choices.label: Ask it to come with you.

success.text: It considers your team: the small ones especially. Then it gets up and stands at the back of them, like a wall. It has decided who it guards.

choices.label: Leave it to guard the water.

success.text: You leave it there, on watch. As you go, the Skiddo settles down in the shade right beside it, and it lets it.

events.name: Shade for Everyone
events.intro: You pass the watering hole again. It doesn't look the same. A stand of young bamboo has grown up all the way round it, and there is shade for everyone.

success.text: Skiddo, Phanpy, a Pangoro or two. Nobody growls. Somebody has planted bamboo, and you can guess who.
